old: Where a movement puts its past. One pendulum swings under a gallows frame at the head of the open south half; every 25 ms its position is kept together with the time it was taken, and drawn behind the bob at 0.6 m per second of age, so the record recedes down the hall toward the exit. Two limits hold the record: 300 marks and 10 s. A panel on the walk-side post switches the sampler (FINE 25 ms, COARSE 200 ms, STROBE once per measured period) and resets this experiment; a cased readout beside the trail prints the count, the span kept, the interval, the depth rate and the period. The seismograph and the Foucault rig keep other records on other clocks. Structure recovered 2026-09-10: interior 2 = platform, perimeter w, wall_height 3.

old:
Walk into a deep amphitheater where the unit circle reveals the origin of all oscillation. A point rotating on a circle projects its shadow as a sine wave. Elevated ramparts frame the void where the unit circle animator floats, while oscillating bridges at the base make the wave physical—the ground moves under your feet. Rotation is the hidden engine behind every sine and cosine.

old: A pendulum with configurable control parameters — adjust damping, driving force, and frequency to explore the transition from periodic motion through quasi-periodicity to chaos. The canonical example of nonlinear dynamics in a physical system.
new: A grabbable pendulum integrates the nonlinear restoring term -(g/L)sin(angle), damping and optional drive. Release position and tangent hand velocity set its next swing. Configured plumb/trace evidence can expose signed centre crossings and a prediction from the standard start; length sets the small-angle period only with gravity fixed.

old: Pendulum generating a sine wave
new: One integrated pendulum leaves a timestamped position record: sample age becomes depth. FINE, COARSE and measured-period STROBE expose physics-tick sampling, a 300-mark budget and a ten-second age limit; RESET restarts this experiment.

old: A passageway bounded by undulating walls—walking through is walking through a frozen wave. The body experiences wavelength as architectural scale.

old: oscillation: the unit circle, annotated — sine and cosine read off a turning radius; the circle that secretly writes every wave.
